newsitem.title: UK: London gold fixes at highest since early July.
newsitem.headline: London gold fixes at highest since early July.

text.p: Gold prices may be about to test levels over $330.00 an ounce for the first time since early July following a fund-led short covering rally last last week, dealers said.
Gold was fixed at $328.05 on Monday, up from $324.20 on Friday and recording the highest fixing since July 3 of $332.55.
That was the day the Reserve Bank of Australia announced it had sold 167 tonnes of gold from its reserves, starting a decline that saw the gold price crash to its lowest level in 12 years.
The slump was driven by the investment funds massively extending short positions in anticipation of prices falling below $300.00.
But that sentiment dissipated last week after physical buying provided a price base between $315.00 and $318.00. A wobble in hitherto rampant U.S. equities last Friday also helped gold.
Some dealers and market analysts said the bounce was to be expected as gold had become extremely oversold, but the extent to which the bounce could continue was debatable.
"Most dealers expected it to get to $328.00 this morning but be turned back there. Now it has pushed past that and $330.00 is possible, but nobody is too sure anymore," one dealer said.
He added that physical enquiry was in the market at current prices, but on an inter-dealer basis sellers were reluctant.
Fund profit-taking from short positions was largely behind the fall of Comex open interest last Thursday by over 3,000 lots to 219,005 lots.
The open interest had been at its highest for 18 months earlier in the week. The data for last Friday will be released late Monday and analysts forecast a further fall.
"The idea last month that going short was the correct decision hasn't suddenly become wrong," one market analyst said.
He added that further fund short covering was likely but the possibility of them re-opening shorts was high as well.
"What is encouraging for gold is that gold shares went up when Wall Street came down," the analyst added.
The other precious metals were firmer as well, partially marked up with gold as interest was sparse.
Silver was indicated at $4.31/$4.33, up two cents and very quiet.
Platinum at $412.00/$415.00 was $6.00 ahead of Friday's close and palladium was $4.50 ahead at $188.00/$191.00.
